name: Footprints Healing Centre — Alexander First Nation
description: NNADAP-funded residential addiction treatment centre on Alexander First Nation near Morinville. Offers a culturally grounded healing program for adults 18+ with 12 in-patient beds and an average 42-day treatment cycle. Programs include concurrent disorders treatment, residential school trauma healing, on-the-land programming, couples counselling, AA/NA meetings, cognitive behavioural therapy, a 7-week virtual program, and cultural programming. Accepts pregnant women, court/corrections referrals, clients on psychoactive medications, and child welfare clients. Block intake model.
location: Alexander First Nation, near Morinville, AB
hours_of_operation: Residential program — contact for intake schedule
eligibility: Adults 18+, male and female. Accepts pregnant women, court/corrections referrals, clients on psychoactive medications, and child welfare clients. Must complete NNADAP referral form.

name: Kapown Rehabilitation Centre — Grouard
description: NNADAP-funded 32-bed residential addiction treatment centre on Kapawe'no First Nation near Grouard, on the shore of Buffalo Bay. Operating for over 25 years, Kapown treats approximately 300 clients annually with a comprehensive evidence-based program integrating Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, Solution-Focused Therapy, Mindfulness, Motivationally Enhanced Therapy, and Twelve Step Facilitation with Western Cree cultural practices woven throughout. Programs include concurrent disorders, residential school trauma healing, on-the-land activities, gender-based programming, family treatment, child counselling, couples counselling, prescription drug abuse treatment, aftercare services, and recreation. Also offers out-patient treatment and a 2nd Stage Treatment Program. Counsellors are CACII/ICADC certified.
location: Kapawe'no First Nation, near Grouard, AB
hours_of_operation: Residential program — contact for intake. Toll-free: 1-888-751-3921
eligibility: Adults 18+, male and female. Accepts clients with disabilities, pregnant women, court/corrections referrals, clients on Methadone/Suboxone, and 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals. Continuous intake for in-patient and out-patient programs.

Complete the NNADAP referral form (downloadable from kapown.ca)

wait_times: Continuous intake — contact for current availability

name: Beaver Lake Wah-Pow Treatment Centre
description: NNADAP-funded accredited not-for-profit residential addiction treatment centre on Beaver Lake Cree Nation, 15 km southeast of Lac La Biche. Operating since 1984, the centre provides an intensive 49-day holistic program specializing in the treatment of trauma and abuse for couples and individuals. Cultural programming includes sweat lodge ceremonies, pipe ceremonies, cultural dances, seasonal pow wows, and daily smudging and prayer to support physical, emotional, mental, and spiritual well-being. Offers individual and couples counselling, with couples accommodated in shared cabins. 24-hour security and round-the-clock counselling services on-site.

address: Box 1648, Lac La Biche, AB T0A 2C0

name: Hinton Friendship Centre
description: Aboriginal non-profit organization serving Indigenous and non-Indigenous community members in Hinton and area since 1995. Programs include the Mamowichihitowin inclusive therapy program, Aboriginal Head Start for Indigenous children ages 3-5, Indigenous Language and Culture Program (ILC) teaching Plains Cree, Saulteaux, and Michif at local schools, Restoring Balance wrap-around reintegration program for offenders, teen cooking classes, and cultural programming. Provides holistic support addressing spiritual, emotional, mental, and physical wellness.
eligibility: Open to Indigenous and non-Indigenous community members. Some programs have specific eligibility (e.g., Aboriginal Head Start for Indigenous children 3-5).
process_steps: Call 780-865-5189 or visit the centre at 965 Switzer Drive, Hinton
Staff will assess needs and connect to appropriate programs
No referral required for most programs

name: Cold Lake Native Friendship Centre
description: The only Indigenous organization in the Cold Lake area, serving both Indigenous and non-Indigenous community members. Acts as a cultural support hub providing access to family services, addiction support, food programs, and housing services. Offers on-site counselling, career guidance, youth programs, a weekly Soup and Bannock Thursday community meal, free copying/faxing, resume creation, tax filing assistance, and a Community Temporary Work Agency providing temporary employment opportunities. Currently developing Kokum's House, a culturally relevant recovery program with 10 beds for men, blending Indigenous healing methods with western recovery models including land-based healing and peer mentorship.
eligibility: Open to all Indigenous and non-Indigenous community members. No eligibility requirements for drop-in services.
process_steps: Walk in or call 780-594-7526
Staff will connect you to appropriate services
No referral or documentation required for most services

name: Bent Arrow Traditional Healing Society — Cultural & Family Programs
description: Edmonton-based Indigenous organization serving children, youth, families, and seniors since 1994, dedicated to restoring cultural pride and well-being. Offers a wide range of culturally grounded programs including Sacred Circle family intervention, Elder's counsel and Elder breakfasts, Coyote Kids weekly program, Coyote Pride youth mentoring, White Cloud Head Start, Wind Dancers youth program, Her Way women's program, Warriors Way men's program, Kikosewin Family Resource Network, seniors programming, traditional Indigenous teachings, community outreach, Wichitowin family nights, monthly soup and bannock lunches, Aboriginal awareness training, employment career centre, Journey to Success adult employment, and the Equipped to Work initiative for Indigenous newcomers to Edmonton. Part of the Wellness Network Edmonton.
eligibility: Open to Indigenous community members — children, youth, families, and seniors. Some programs open to all. Contact for specific program eligibility.
